purpose: A staged research program for foundational cybersecurity, advanced security engineering, and current standards. Sources guide hypotheses and controls; they are not proof or policy activation.
scope: The existing Crucible pipeline and its project-bound repositories, workflows, custody stores, workers, dashboards, and release paths.

authoritativeSourcesReviewed.title: Key Management Guidelines (SP 800-57 family)
observations: Protect key material and metadata against disclosure, substitution, and modification.
Treat generation, storage, distribution, rotation, revocation, backup, and destruction as separate governed lifecycle functions.

authoritativeSourcesReviewed.title: SP 800-63-4 Digital Identity Guidelines
observations: Bind authentication and federation to assurance, lifecycle, session, and privacy requirements.

authoritativeSourcesReviewed.title: Secrets Management Cheat Sheet
observations: Centralize storage, provisioning, auditing, rotation, and access control; scope CI/CD identities to only required secrets and services.

authoritativeSourcesReviewed.title: Actions Secure Use Reference
observations: Default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions to read-only, rotate secrets, keep actions current, and avoid granting automation pull-request approval authority.

authoritativeSourcesReviewed.title: Actions OpenID Connect Reference
observations: Use exact repository/ref/audience trust conditions and the minimum id-token permission when replacing long-lived cloud credentials.

authoritativeSourcesReviewed.title: Actions Secrets Reference
observations: Keep secret use within explicit repository or organization scope and do not treat secret names as proof of configured values.

courseraEngineeringResearch.title: Coding assistants with review, testing, and secure boundaries

courseSources.title: Generative AI Coding Assistants for Developers

syllabusObservations: AI assistance is useful for suggestions, refactoring, debugging, documentation, testing, and collaborative review.
Assistant output still requires human review, security checks, tests, provenance, and repository policy enforcement.
courseraEngineeringResearch.crucibleApplication: Use assistants only as bounded proposal generators; require route checks, diff review, focused tests, security scans, exact-tip verification, and no credential or custody access.
developmentTests: Reject assistant-generated changes without tests or provenance
Require secret and executable-content scans before retention
Compare assistant proposal against the task boundary and changed-path route

courseraEngineeringResearch.title: Hypothesis-driven debugging and regression repair

courseSources.title: Writing, Running, and Fixing Code in C

syllabusObservations: Use a scientific, hypothesis-driven workflow, profiling, observability, and structured root-cause analysis.
A bug fix should be paired with a reproducer and regression test.
courseraEngineeringResearch.crucibleApplication: Require deterministic reproduction, smallest safe repair, negative test, regression test, and exact failure/run lineage; never mask a failure by weakening a gate.
developmentTests: Reproduce a known bug before editing
Require a failing test then a passing regression test
Reject fixes that alter unrelated paths or suppress the original failure

courseraEngineeringResearch.title: Measured optimization and scalability
syllabusObservations: Optimization topics include profiling, caching, asynchronous work, scalability, query and code bottlenecks, and before/after comparison.
AI suggestions for optimization must be measured rather than accepted by intuition.
courseraEngineeringResearch.crucibleApplication: Add benchmark baselines and resource budgets only where a measured bottleneck exists; preserve correctness, security, determinism, and evidence custody.
developmentTests: Require reproducible before/after measurements
Reject an optimization that regresses correctness, security, memory, or tail latency
Verify cache invalidation and asynchronous failure handling

courseraEngineeringResearch.title: Testing strategy, automation, and regression coverage

courseSources.title: Foundations of Software Testing and Validation

syllabusObservations: Use layered unit, integration, system, acceptance, security, performance, regression, smoke, mutation, and soak testing.
Test plans and precise bug reports improve repeatability and historical traceability.
courseraEngineeringResearch.crucibleApplication: Extend the existing focused-to-integration-to-broad cadence with claim-specific negative tests, regression coverage, mutation checks, and exact hosted evidence without weakening required checks.
developmentTests: Require every repair to add or reference a regression test
Exercise negative, mutation, concurrency, soak, and rollback cases where the boundary warrants them
Reject skipped required tests and stale exact-tip results

courseraEngineeringResearch.title: Application-security testing and secure bug repair
syllabusObservations: Combines manual and automated security testing, attacker thinking, and systematic debugging.
Security testing should be integrated into the delivery workflow rather than deferred to release.
courseraEngineeringResearch.crucibleApplication: Route security findings into candidate learning with exact signatures, reproduction, remediation ownership, and verification; never turn a course claim into active policy.
developmentTests: Run security tests against changed boundaries
Require a reproducible finding and a distinct verifier for remediation
Preserve redacted evidence and reject unsupported security claims

findings: Coding assistance should accelerate proposals, not authorize mutations.
Optimization must be measurement-led and must not trade away correctness, security, or provenance.
Bug fixing needs reproducible failure, bounded repair, regression evidence, and recurrence review.
Testing quality improves when claim-specific negative, regression, mutation, soak, and hosted exact-tip checks are explicit.
The same evidence contract should span discovery through release: exact inputs, bounded effects, redacted lineage, independent verification, and fail-closed behavior.
developmentTests: Trace one change from task route through test, hosted run, artifact provenance, and release decision
Reject missing lineage or unauthorized cross-boundary writes
Compare performance, reliability, security, and learning metrics before and after a bounded change

knowledgeIsPower.principle: Knowledge increases the ability to predict, coordinate, and act; it does not by itself establish truth, wisdom, permission, or moral authority.
knowledgeIsPower.crucibleApplication: Require provenance, uncertainty, reproducibility, source independence, and scoped authorization before an observation can influence a governed action.

powerCorruptsWithoutAccountability.principle: Concentrated authority without independent review, equal standards, dissent, or revocation creates incentives for self-justification and unchecked error.
powerCorruptsWithoutAccountability.crucibleApplication: No worker, dashboard, verifier, or evidence packet may authorize its own promotion; retain independent verification, owner approval, kill-switch, rollback, and immutable audit lineage.

philosophyAndGovernance.designRule: Knowledge may inform action; it may not authorize itself.

immediateImprovement.description: Make the existing evidence packet operational by correlating redacted runtime events across every component boundary with exact input/output digests, actor, status, failure reason, and rollback reference.
immediateImprovement.successMeasure: A controlled failure produces one complete, secret-free trace from route through verification and rollback without granting promotion authority.

architectureQualityContract.principle: Architecture decisions must expose quality trade-offs and ethical impact before implementation; no architecture packet grants promotion authority.

officialSources.title: Create and modify scripts by using Windows PowerShell

syllabusObservations: Prioritize JavaScript and TypeScript because the active Crucible implementation is JavaScript-heavy and its typed interfaces, async behavior, and test contracts affect nearly every boundary.
Use Python and Java for extraction, data, and verifier tooling; use C, C++, and C# for native-toolchain, memory-safety, and cross-language fixture coverage.
Use PowerShell and shell for Windows/CI automation, but require explicit path handling, input validation, error propagation, signing, and fail-closed behavior.
Treat HTML, CSS, React, and React Native as dashboard/operator-surface skills, with accessibility, authentication boundaries, state handling, and no secret exposure.
Treat JSON as a data-contract and canonicalization skill, not as a general-purpose programming language; validate schemas, hashes, provenance, and rejection behavior.
Use Django as a Python web-stack profile only where a real service boundary exists; verify ORM, authentication, CSRF, migrations, and deployment behavior independently.
furtherResearch.crucibleApplication: Add course and official-document links as candidate research inputs to the existing pipeline; map each language to concrete fixture, scanner, compiler, parser, or verifier tests and retain the current no-substitution rule for unavailable harnesses.
developmentTests: Verify every catalog profile has an explicit extension mapping, source-language fixture, and distinct experiment/verifier path before a claim can advance.
Reject a language-learning claim when the named compiler, runtime, parser, or harness is unavailable; never substitute another language.
Add negative tests for shell/PowerShell injection, JSON canonicalization and schema confusion, web authentication/CSRF boundaries, and native memory/FFI hazards where applicable.
Compare course-derived hypotheses against official language/runtime documentation and independent controlled tests before durable retention.
